messages.subject: Re: Problematic bifactor model
parts:
In bfactor(), use NA place holders in the first model argument for items that have no specific factor. For the general, your form above is fine. So something like 

mod <- 'G =  1-4,6,7,9-25'
vec <- c(1,1,1,2,2,NA,1,2, ...)
bfactor(data, vec, mod)

HTH.

Phil


On Fri, Jul 13, 2018 at 5:59 PM Danilo Assis Pereira <dani...@gmail.com> wrote:
Is it possible to do a bifactor model like this one? The problem here is that some items are not in the specific factors and two of them are not in the general factor. If it is possible, how to do it?

mod <- 'F1 = 4,16,18,24
F2 = 1,11,14,15,17,20,22,25
F3 = 2,3,5,8
G = 1-4,6,7,9-25' #without items 5 and 8

Thanks a lot.
